item.title: Overgrown Brambles & Hedges, 24th October
item.description:
There's a stretch of pavement between Fox Close and Otter Road on Lobleys Drive that is becoming incredibly overgrown and difficult to pass, especially by the bus stop. The brambles are hanging down, which not only causes dangers to pedestrians (especially children), they also force you to walk on the grass. With the weather turning, the verges are becoming very muddy which is then spreading onto the pavement - another hazard because it's becoming slippery. A previous reported stated highways had taken action, but all they did was remove a couple of brambles hanging down directly over the path. But it's that whole stretch that needs to be significantly cut back and tidied up. We should have to duck or dodge to avoid the hedges. I'm often out walking with two children in a pushchair and two large dogs (as one photo shows) and it's becoming increasingly difficult to get past in certain areas. Please can this be sorted as soon as possible, and I suspect it'll only get worse over winter.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Lobleys Drive, Abbeymead, Gloucester
Report on FixMyStreet
